rules.description: Applicant or someone in the household must be disabled
rules.reason_if_failed: This grant is for disabled people who need home adaptations. You must have a physical disability, learning disability, age-related needs, autism, cognitive impairment, progressive condition, terminal illness, or mental health condition.

rules.description: Disabled person must intend to live in the property during the grant period (usually 5 years)
rules.reason_if_failed: The disabled person must intend to live in the property for at least 5 years (or shorter period if terminally ill).

rules.description: Applicant must be owner, tenant, or landlord of the property
rules.reason_if_failed: You must be the property owner, tenant, or landlord to apply for this grant.

rules.description: Property must be in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland
rules.reason_if_failed: Disabled Facilities Grants are not available in Scotland. Find out about support for equipment and adaptations from your local council.

rules.description: Work must not have started before council approval
rules.reason_if_failed: You might not get any grant if you start work on your property before the council approves your application.

rules.description: For adults over 18, household income and savings over £6,000 will be assessed
rules.reason_if_failed: N/A - this is an assessment rule, not a rejection criterion

rules.description: Work must be necessary and appropriate to meet disabled person's needs
rules.reason_if_failed: The occupational therapist assessment found that the proposed work is not necessary or appropriate to meet your needs.

rules.description: Work must be reasonable given the age and condition of the property
rules.reason_if_failed: The council has determined that the proposed work is not reasonable given the age and condition of your property.

explanation_template: Disabled Facilities Grant eligibility: {outcome}. Maximum grant: £30,000 (England), £36,000 (Wales), £25,000 (Northern Ireland). Means test applies unless under 18 or landlord application.

edge_cases.description: Disabled child under 18 - no parental means test
edge_cases.action: Skip means test. Grant based solely on need, not household income or savings.
Skip means test. Council may require property to be let to another disabled person if tenant moves within 5 years.

edge_cases.description: Applicant or disabled person has terminal illness
edge_cases.action: Grant period can be shorter than 5 years. Expedite assessment and decision process.

edge_cases.description: Applying for another grant for the same property due to condition change
edge_cases.action: Allowed. Assess changed needs and whether previous adaptations are still appropriate.

edge_cases.description: Work requires planning permission or building regulations approval
edge_cases.action: Applicant must apply separately for planning permission. Council may require qualified architect or surveyor. Grant can cover their fees.
Application likely to be rejected. Refer to council appeals process.
